newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Sept 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Sept 19.

text.p: Copper prices rose strongly overnight and other metals rose in response. Wheat rose on signals the market was oversold while oil rose along with heating oil prices and reports of Iraqi shelling of Kurds.
The CRB index ended 1.49 points higher at 245.89.

Copper prices rose strongly, boosted by U.S.-led gains late on Tuesday and follow-through short-covering in subdued trade. Other base metals rose in response as some confidence returned to what was recently decribed as an overwhelmingly bearish LME.

Benchmark three month LME copper futures ended the afternoon kerb at $1,925 a tonne, up $55 from Tuesday's afternoon kerb close and at the high of the day. Traders were looking for more short term gains, with the next upside target pegged at $1,950.
Aluminium gained $13.50 to $1,433. "The aluminium market was well oversold and due for a bounce," said one trader.
Zinc rose in the wake of the firmer overall trend, adding $16 to $1,041. Sizeable falls in stocks were lending background support, although Wednesday's rally was more short-covering.
Lead gained $16 to $788, paring some of the recent heavy losses. On the charts lead closed back above an important rising trendline below which prices slumped during Tuesday's sell-off.

Strong commercial stopping of the deliveries posted against the September contract and signals the wheat market was oversold boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close. "Wheat already was beat up and the funds were short plus Continental stopped the wheat," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Nearby September, set to expire at on Thursday, was strong because of the aggressive commercial demand.
Wheat closed 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher to two lower, with September up 9-1/2 at $4.32-1/2.

NYMEX October crude oil closed up 58 cents to $23.89 a barrel, following heating oil higher though a report of Iraqi shelling of Kurdish refugees also bolstered prices. Wednesday's rise in crude followed heavy selling days earlier.

Sugar closed barely changed after speculative selling stymied an early attempt to rally. Most-active March closed up 0.02 at 11.30, having ranged from 11.35 to 11.26. Spot-October eased 0.03 on the day to finish at 11.40, barely above the low of 11.40.
